pairs.difference: A: the chip is seen from high above and almost straight down. The board sits small and fully framed in the middle of a plain off-white tabletop. The pins on all four sides look nearly the same size, so there is almost no foreshortening. B: the book is turned 3/4 and fills the card, with its corner cut by the bottom-right edge. Its spine and page block foreshorten strongly toward the back right, and the wood-grain floor recedes with the book.
pairs.fix: Turn the chip about 30° so one corner points at the viewer. Use a lower 3/4 camera so the near pins look bigger than the far ones. Make the chip fill most of the card and let the table surface run off the edges.

pairs.difference: A: the helmet is shown nearly front-on at eye level and sits small in the middle. It rests on a seamless purple backdrop with no clear floor line: the floor fades into the wall behind a soft shadow. B: the sneakers sit on a clear floor plane with a sharp wall/floor horizon line. The left shoe overlaps the right one, and both are shown in a consistent 3/4 view.
pairs.fix: Turn the helmet 3/4 so the visor faces off to one side. Stand it on a visible floor that meets a back wall at a clear horizon line. Move the camera closer so the helmet fills the card.

pairs.difference: A: the flask is seen straight on from a low camera. Its symmetric silhouette sits on a metal counter whose front edge is cropped at the bottom. The counter top is a thin sliver, so the camera is almost at counter height. B: the locker is turned 3/4 with its door swung toward the viewer. The floor boards and the baseboard recede at the same angle, and the door overlaps the shelf.
pairs.fix: Raise the camera a little and turn the flask so the counter top shows as a clear receding surface. Turn the counter edge on a diagonal instead of running it parallel to the card's bottom edge.

pairs.difference: A: the plane comes toward the viewer in a dynamic 3/4 view. The nose and near engine are big, the tail is small, and the wings are cut off by the card edges. B: the UFO floats small in the middle, seen from slightly above, with its disc reading as a flat ellipse. Nothing overlaps the frame, and the clouds sit as flat bands with no depth relation to the saucer.
pairs.fix: Tilt the saucer and bring it closer so its near rim is noticeably bigger than the far rim. Let part of the disc break past one card edge, and put a cloud in front of the saucer so there is a foreground layer.

pairs.difference: A: the camera is close and low. The bike and car fill the card and are cropped on three sides, with the road and hills compressed behind them. B: the rover is shown whole and small in the middle, seen from above at a 3/4 angle. A wide moon plain stretches to a far horizon dotted with rocks, and there is a lot of empty ground around the vehicle.
pairs.fix: Move the camera down and in so the rover fills the card and its near wheel is cut by the bottom edge. Keep the moon horizon low and simple, and drop the scattered rocks spread across the empty ground.

pairs.difference: A: the rocket is drawn on a diagonal, nearly side-on. Both fins are flat plates with no turn, and the round window is a perfect circle facing the camera, so the body has no foreshortening. B: the balloons overlap front to back. The middle balloon covers the ones behind it, which separates the layers.
pairs.fix: Turn the rocket so the nose comes slightly toward the viewer. Show the near fin bigger and the far fin partly hidden behind the body, and draw the window as an oval that wraps around the curve.

pairs.difference: A: the column is seen close and from slightly below, cropped on three edges. The room corner and plinth set a consistent 3/4 perspective. B: the arch is seen straight on and symmetric, standing on a flat floor line. The view is frontal but consistent, much like the frontal real cards (the clock). Neither card breaks its own view.

A: the vault door is drawn straight on as a flat wall plate. Yet its hinges stick out sideways and the floor strip at the bottom tilts, so the wall and floor do not share one view. The left wall edge curves away as if from a wide-angle lens. B: the gate has a consistent 3/4 view. The paving stones recede toward the gate, and the brick pillars foreshorten correctly.
pairs.fix: Show the vault door set into a wall turned slightly to one side. Make the hinges and the floor line follow the same angle, and keep the wall edges straight, with no curved wide-angle bend.

pairs.difference: A: the console sits whole and centered on a steel counter, seen from slightly above. The counter edge runs on a mild diagonal, and the screen panel faces the camera flat while the base turns, so the two parts sit at slightly different angles. B: the claw machine has one consistent 3/4 view. The floor tiles and the room corner recede together, and the glass box shows the inside depth.
pairs.fix: Turn the whole console, screen and base together, as one block at a 3/4 angle. Bring the camera closer so the console fills the card and the counter runs off both side edges.

pairs.difference: A: the stone table is seen from a 3/4 high angle on grass that recedes to trees and a path, with the stool overlapping the table. B: the target booth is seen straight on, with the teddy bear overlapping the target. Each card keeps one view and has clear foreground, hero and background layers.

A: the fan is seen close and cropped at the bottom. It is placed in a room corner with a curtain, which gives three clear depth layers. B: the dish is shown whole on a bare concrete slab. The slab meets the sky at a flat horizon with nothing between them, and the hero sits centered with empty ground around it.
pairs.fix: Bring the camera closer and lower so the dish fills the card and its base is cut by the bottom edge. Add a simple background layer behind the slab, such as a railing or rooftop edge, instead of a bare horizon.

pairs.difference: A: the ring box is seen from above at a 3/4 angle. Its lid tips back and the cushion foreshortens, so the object clearly sits in depth and fills the card. B: the satellite floats small in the middle, almost front-on. The two solar panels are flat rectangles of the same size facing the camera, so there is almost no foreshortening, and a lot of empty starburst surrounds it.
pairs.fix: Turn the satellite 3/4 so one solar panel comes toward the viewer and looks bigger while the other recedes and shrinks. Bring it closer so the near panel breaks past the card edge.

pattern: The generated cards usually show the hero whole, small and centered, with a flat front-on or straight-down view and little foreshortening. They also leave empty ground or sky around the hero and give a bare horizon instead of layered depth. The real cards use a closer 3/4 camera that crops the frame edges, makes near parts bigger than far parts, and keeps all parts and the ground in one view.
